cells.tense: Right now, you are holding more true things than most people can carry at once.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: In the work you're refining, lay out once how it all fits — plainly, before anyone asks you to. Out loud if someone's there, on paper if not. Don't go back to tighten the wording afterward.
cells.core:
You can hold several true things at once without flattening them into one, and you do it in a room where you're building skill by repetition. Nothing you take up gets simplified behind its back. Colleagues come to you with half-formed things and leave with the parts still intact. In a practice that rewards narrowing, yours stays whole.

When you see how something fits, lay out the shape of it once, before anyone asks, and don't go back to tighten the wording afterward. You'll want to wait until it's tighter first. Waiting is the habit here, and it's the one that costs. So does holding back: what stays inside lands half-finished, and the saying is where it finishes.
cells.sheetLine: You hold more than one true thing without dropping any.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once and keeping them true
cells.place: a solitary bench where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: Ahead of you, every path this could take is already being held open at once.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Name the direction in the work that matters most to you, and work only that for three days — no checking on the others, no keeping them warm. Then see which went quiet.
cells.core:
In the work you're refining, you can see every direction it could still go, and you're keeping them all available — nothing gets to close. It reads as thoroughness. From the bench, it looks like nothing is being built, because building means some of them end.

Name the direction that matters most, and give it three days alone. No surveying the others, no keeping them warm. By the third day some will look dark, and you'll want to check on them — that pull is the thing to let loosen. What you've cultivated in the one you kept shines because it's finished being possible.
cells.sheetLine: Everything stays open, so nothing gets built.

cells.tense: The door you were standing at in this work has already closed behind you.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Do a piece of this work with one other person at the same time — one session, the same task, not beside each other. Watch what the work does with two in it.
cells.core:
In this work, things used to come to you directly, and now they arrive with an argument attached. You stand outside the practice, going through the motions of something that stopped being yours a while back. Building skill by repetition means being inside it; you've been at the door.

Don't try to want it back by yourself — that's what's been failing. Do one piece of this work with someone, not next to them: the same task, at the same time. What you stopped seeing is easier to catch with another person in it. Let it be lighter than doing it alone. Whatever returns comes back through the shared part first.

cells.tense: You are settling what is fair in this work, and if asked, you'd call it nothing much.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Settle a debt inside the work you're refining — to a person in it, or to the work itself — where nobody's watching. For a week after, don't count what's owed back to you.
cells.core:
Where you're refining skill by repetition, you keep things even — what's owed, what's too much to ask — and you act on it without ceremony. Your sense of right is accurate, and it steadies the room. Nobody has put your name on it.

Settle what's owed inside this work, quietly, where nobody sees — to a person in it or to the work itself, whichever is nearest. For a week after, don't count what comes back to you. The fairness you keep following is yours; doing it once by hand is what signs it. Meet it yourself and the account closes with no one thanking you, which is exactly how you wanted it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep things fair here and file it under luck.
